# NPM Improved v1.6.7 — Private-host ACME validation and clear certificate errors

## ACME and access lists
- Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 challenge URLs remain accessible even when the proxy host is protected by an access list such as **GG Private**. Access control remains enforced for all ordinary application requests.
- Fix the forced-HTTPS exception so it covers **all valid ACME challenge tokens**, not only the static test token.
- Eliminate temporary duplicate Nginx virtual hosts during HTTP-01 issuance. Reuse the dedicated NPMX-aware ACME handler on each node instead, without temporarily disabling the protected proxy host.
- Package the updated forced-SSL Nginx include into the actual production image.

## Plain-English errors
- Display actionable details from the current Certbot attempt in the API and UI: the hostname, responding node/IP, and 403 (forbidden), 404 (missing challenge), 401 (authentication required), redirect, timeout, DNS, or rate-limit category.
- Do not expose ACME challenge tokens, provider credentials, full log lines, or private error stacks.
- Keep full details in server logs for further troubleshooting.

## Verification
- GitHub backend, Docker, Required Checks, and Repository Health workflows passed on the fix PR.
- Local Nginx smoke testing confirmed ACME requests succeed while private routes remain restricted and forced-HTTPS still redirects ordinary requests.
- Update the NPMX primary first and then all secondaries. Test the same ACME token against every public proxy IP before requesting a production certificate.
